Looking at the net, the six triangles in the middle strip wrap around to form the "band" of the octahedron (like an antiprism), with the left edge D joining the right edge A. This means the top row vertices wrap so that the leftmost and rightmost top points coincide, and likewise for the bottom row.

- The top flap (with edges C and the blue edge) folds over to close the top triangle: its edge C meets the top boundary edge B.
- The bottom flap (with edges x and the blue edge) folds over to close the bottom triangle: its vertex meets the middle bottom vertex, so edge x (from the right bottom point to the flap tip) closes up exactly onto the bottom boundary edge from the left bottom point to the middle bottom point — the edge labelled E.

Checking the pairs: D↔A, C↔B, and x↔E.
